history.title: Fault-Check Gate Split Data Hall

style_when: the article describes one decisive moment or place — a yard at dawn, a control room, a shutdown line, a handover — that a film still could hold
prompt: A wide anamorphic 35mm film still in a double-height data hall, split-screen diptych divided by a vertical brushed-steel seam. Left half: a tidy server rack row glowing green status LEDs, polished concrete floor, deep shadows. Right half: an identical rack row behind a heavy steel fault-check gate, padlocked, dark except one red status light above an empty repair bay, scuffed concrete. Hard overhead fluorescent light from above-left, graphite and steel blue with safety-yellow and oxidised-red accents, fine film grain, no text, no logos, no people.
negative_prompt: garbled text, random letters, watermarks, labels, UI, readable words
rationale: The article describes a decisive operational environment—a live cluster where a fix is either authenticated by an external check or rejected. A cinematic still can stage the data hall with industrial atmosphere and a split-screen contrast, making the verification barrier tangible without falling back to generic datacenter filler.
subject: a heavy steel fault-check gate dividing a server row between green diagnosis and dark unverified recovery
core_thesis: Verified recovery, not root-cause accuracy, is the gate an incident agent must pass.
core_conflict: Detection runs 72.7% to 99.7% while a valid, executed fix lands 14.5% to 60.3%, and invalid plans miss on the operation (67.9%) rather than the service.
composition: split-screen diptych with left-right detection-vs-recovery contrast
alt_text: A steel gate with a padlock divides a lit server aisle from a dark data hall.
caption: Your Agent's Fix Fails: autonomy needs a fault-reproducing check, not the agent's own report.
title: Incident Agent Fixes Fail 39.5%

review.depicts: A server room is divided by a steel bar gate with a padlock, with a lit aisle of racks showing green lights on the left and a dimmer aisle of racks with red lights and yellow cables on the right.
review.reason: The frame shows the article's own mechanism—a fault-check gate separating green diagnosis from dark, unverified recovery in server infrastructure.

input.prompt:
A wide anamorphic 35mm film still in a double-height data hall, split-screen diptych divided by a vertical brushed-steel seam. Left half: a tidy server rack row glowing green status LEDs, polished concrete floor, deep shadows. Right half: an identical rack row behind a heavy steel fault-check gate, padlocked, dark except one red status light above an empty repair bay, scuffed concrete. Hard overhead fluorescent light from above-left, graphite and steel blue with safety-yellow and oxidised-red accents, fine film grain, no text, no logos, no people.

Do not include: people, faces, hands, garbled text, random lettering, numbers, signage, watermarks, UI, logos.
